title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-diego-morales
content:
Quick dump of my PR review notes and follow-ups for PR #4721 (kv-cache batching refactor). Use this as my scratchpad for comments to post.

Summary:
- PR changes: centralize KV-cache lifetime management, introduce continuous batching config, move batching logic into runtime scheduler module. Big surface area: scheduler, kv-cache, grpc request path, tests.
- Motivation: reduce duplicate cache population, avoid stalls on cold-start for long contexts, allow adaptive batch sizes per model.

High-level concerns to validate:
1) Correctness: Are we preserving KV-cache coherence across warm restarts and model switch? Need to walk through cases where request is preempted and KV entries are partially written.
2) Concurrency: scheduler now mutates cache from multiple worker threads — check locks/fences, potential READER_STARVATION on low-latency paths.
3) Performance: measure token latency p50/p95 with new batching; ensure tail latency not regressed for small seq lengths.

Concrete review checklist (postable comments):
- [ ] Add unit tests for concurrent cache writes (simulate interleaved write+read).
- [ ] Add integration test: long-seq followed by burst of short-seq to ensure eviction/retention semantics.
- [ ] Document config knobs: batching.min_size, batching.max_latency_ms, scheduler.max_workers. Where are defaults chosen?
- [ ] Replace ad-hoc sleep in scheduler tests with condition variable to avoid flakiness.
- [ ] Annotate TODOs left in src/scheduler/worker_pool.rs lines ~120-140 and explain plan or remove.

Detailed notes / TODOs for author:
- line src/kv_cache/mod.rs: handle_missing_prefix() seems to catch and swallow errors — why not bubble up? Need justification in comment. If intentional, add a metric.
- scheduler/src/scheduler.rs: use of Arc<Mutex<>> around BatchQueue — evaluate if parking_lot::RwLock would be cheaper for read-heavy workloads. Add benchmark note.
- grpc/src/handler.rs: there's a path that bypasses cache lookup when request.metadata.include_cache=false. Confirm callers set that flag for tests only; potential security vector if untrusted metadata allowed.
- docs: update runtime/operational.md with example of tuning batching.* for small models.

Follow-ups (post-merge / follow-up PRs):
- Add a stress test harness that drops random packets and simulates worker restarts (run in CI nightly). Ticket INF-4800.
- Telemetry: emit cache_hit_ratio per-model, and batching_batch_size histograms.
- Ops runbook blurb describing how to rollback to previous scheduler if tail latency spikes.

Notes to self:
- Reproduce locally using docker-compose with model=llama-7b, length=4096; run loadgen with mixed sequence lengths.
- Reach out to Leah about failing e2e on staging; she saw a 12% p95 regress. Might be due to failing metric instrumentation.
- Make comment asking author to add brief explanation for choice of exponential backoff in batch flush (line ~210).

Unresolved questions to ask in review:
- Why was cache entry TTL reduced from 30m to 5m in this PR? That seems aggressive for token reuse.
- Can we decouple batch creation from worker threads to a single dispatcher to reduce contention?

Scratch ideas (brainstorm):
- Consider hierarchical caches: per-worker small fast cache + shared KV to reduce lock contention. Trade-offs: stale reads, complexity.
- Explore lock-free single-writer multiple-reader ring-buffer for BatchQueue. Might help p95 but riskier.

Links to reference PRs / notes:
- Previous batching attempt: PR#4120 (notes in Confluence page above).
- Load tests: GH actions artifact "loadgen-2024-10-20.zip" (see GH PR artifacts).

Plan for final review message: combine checklist above into numbered comments; flag critical correctness/concurrency items as blockers, performance items as must-measure. Keep non-blocking refactors as suggestions.

End of scratchpad.

-- Diego
